messages.subject: Multilevel analysis
parts:
Dear Terrence,

I understand that I can use the method specified on this page to run Multilevel analysis. My question is: may I run the multilevel analysis without specifying the regression? 

I managed to get the model fit using the just syntax below, and I would just like to confirm that I am on the right track. Thanks and I look forward to hearing from you!

1. Model

model <- '

fw1 =~ FCT1 + FCT2 + FCT3 + FCT4 + FCT5 + FCT6

fw2 =~ ICT1 + ICT2 + ICT3 + ICT4 + ICT5 + ICT6


fb1 =~ FCT1 + FCT2 + FCT3 + FCT4 + FCT5 + FCT6

fb2 =~ ICT1 + ICT2 + ICT3 + ICT4 + ICT5 + ICT6'


2. Model fit

fit <- sem(model = model, data = raw, cluster = "cluster")

summary(fit, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized = TRUE)


Regards,

Meng

messages.author: f1530326ce101401
messages.subject: Re: Multilevel analysis
parts:
Hello Meng

I know it is not addressed to me, but I guess trying to help is not the worst thing one can do. It looks fine to me, however I would add 'level : 1' and 'level : 2' (see adjusted model syntax below) because you must specify a model for each level. It seems to make a difference (though I do not know much more about it).

adjusted model syntax:

model <- '

level : 1

fw1 =~ FCT1 + FCT2 + FCT3 + FCT4 + FCT5 + FCT6

fw2 =~ ICT1 + ICT2 + ICT3 + ICT4 + ICT5 + ICT6

fb1 =~ FCT1 + FCT2 + FCT3 + FCT4 + FCT5 + FCT6

fb2 =~ ICT1 + ICT2 + ICT3 + ICT4 + ICT5 + ICT6'

I think you can try to run the multilevel analysis without specifying the regressions (if that is your goal). In that case you would perform a multilevel CFA instead of a multilevel SEM analysis. I am not an expert on this matter, so confirmation from someone else would be great!

Best wishes,

Jasper Bogaert
